title: D.C. Council weighs rules for AI, technology in schools
source_used: AOL.com (local TV report by JT Key) and Hoodline (citing The Washington Informer); WUSA9 page blocked
key_facts: A D.C. Council committee (Committee of the Whole) held a hearing on Friday 9 Oct 2026 on how schools use technology, AI and screen time.
More than 150 people signed up to speak, including school leaders and student advocates.
Council Chair Phil Mendelson said concern is growing about how much of the school day is spent on screens and what it means for learning and wellbeing.
Tech advocates say students must learn to use AI; critics, including the parent group Schools Beyond Screens DC, say tools such as AI tutors are experimental and unregulated.
Hoodline, citing The Washington Informer, says the parent group is pushing for a pause on student-facing generative AI tools.
The hearing came after the Frederick County School Board voted to ban student AI use from pre-K through 12th grade, over cheating and critical-thinking concerns.
quote_evidence: A D.C. Council committee is looking into the use of artificial intelligence and screen time in schools.

More than 150 people signed up to speak during the hearing Friday morning as the committee looked into how schools are using technology and how screen time is being monitored and balanced with other instruction.
The meeting comes after the Frederick County School Board voted to ban the use of AI for students across all grade levels, from pre-K through 12th grade.
why_it_matters_hint: Local lawmakers are weighing limits on AI and screens in schools, but nothing has been decided.
notes: WUSA9 (403) not readable. AOL carries an unattributed local TV-style report by JT Key (outlet not named), so the entry is credited to AI News Desk, naming AOL.com and Hoodline. No rule or vote yet.
